For "redo experiment N with the new workflow" requests: outputs go in `experiments/<N>/Fable/`,
each iteration saved as `experiment_NN_fable_vXX.py` + `experiment_NN_fable_vXX_blender_view_YY.png`
(mirrors the `ChatGPT 5.1/` folder naming), rendered headless with Blender 4.3 at
`C:/Program Files/Blender Foundation/Blender 4.3/blender.exe` (5.1 also installed, untested).
Renders must be shaded with object outlines on (coplanar pieces distinguishable); add close-up /
layer-hidden views freely. Max 10 model iterations; minimise questions; consult `input/` manuals
for construction questions; archive the session transcript (copy the `.jsonl` into the folder).

**Why:** Luka works as architect/reviewer and wants to compare LLM runs side by side with the
earlier ChatGPT workflow, including the full conversation.

**How to apply:** Reuse `experiments/13_.../Fable/render_fable.py` as the renderer template; pass an
absolute output prefix (Blender resolves relative paths against its own cwd). See
[[craftbot-project-overview]] if it exists.

Since experiment 02 (2026-08-22) `render_fable.py` also runs a SAT box-box overlap check after rendering (prints penetrating pairs > 1 mm); reuse `experiments/02_Carport_Gothic_Blender_Python/Fable/render_fable.py` when the model is all `place_element` boxes — it catches joint errors the renders hide.

Experiment 03 (2026-08-22): `experiments/03_VIPP_Shelter_Blender_Python/Fable/` has the most general versions of the helpers (`get_collection` nested paths, `box()` from corner coords, `stud_wall` with door/window openings + noggins, `tile_sheets`/`clad_x` plywood tiling) and a renderer with the SAT check — start new box-only experiments from there. Heredocs containing apostrophes break the Bash tool on Windows; use the Write tool for scripts.

Claude Code transcripts (`~/.claude/projects/.../<session>.jsonl`) store messages, tool calls
and tool results but thinking blocks are redacted (empty string + signature). Luka wants to
reconstruct the design thinking of each experiment run later, so: (1) narrate decisions,
rejected alternatives and key numbers in visible text as you go; (2) finish each run with a
`experiment_NN_<model>_design_rationale.md` in the output folder, using
`experiments/13_Hip_Roof_Sheathing_Blender_Python/Fable/experiment_13_fable_design_rationale.md`
as the template (its §0 lists the sections; extend as needed) — one document only, no separate notes file; (3) copy the session `.jsonl`
into the output folder as the **last** step (and remind that `/export` gives a markdown copy).

**Why:** Asked explicitly on 2026-08-21 after discovering the archived jsonl had no reasoning.

**How to apply:** Applies to every craftbot experiment run; see [[headless-blender-iteration-workflow]].

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# CRAFT BOT - Blender Python geometry functions
# V 1.1
# ------------------------------------------------------------------


# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# MODULE IMPORTS

import bpy
import math
from mathutils import Matrix, Vector



# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# GEOMETRY CREATION


def place_element(
        name,
        loc=(0.0, 0.0, 0.0),
        axis=(0.0, 0.0, 1.0),
        angle=0.0,
        scale=(1.0, 1.0, 1.0),
        euler=None,
        euler_order='XYZ',
        matrix=None,
    ):
    """
    Create (or replace) a cube called `name` and place it in the scene.

    You can control the transform in three different ways, in this order
    of priority:

    1) Full matrix (most explicit)
       - Pass `matrix` as a 4×4 world-space transform (mathutils.Matrix
         or a 4×4 nested sequence).
       - All other transform parameters (loc, axis, angle, scale, euler,
         euler_order) are ignored in this case.

    2) Euler angles (more convenient for many users)
       - Pass `euler=(rx, ry, rz)` in *radians* and optionally
         `euler_order='XYZ'` (or any valid Blender Euler order).
       - `loc` and `scale` are still used.

    3) Axis + angle (backwards compatible default)
       - If `matrix` is None and `euler` is None, the function falls
         back to the original behavior:
         * `axis` is the rotation axis in world space.
         * `angle` is the rotation angle in *degrees*.
         * `loc` and `scale` are used as before.

    Parameters
    ----------
    name : str
        Blender object name. Existing object with this name will be replaced.
    loc : 3-tuple or Vector
        World-space location of the object (translation).
    axis : 3-tuple or Vector
        Rotation axis in world space (used only if euler and matrix are None).
    angle : float
        Rotation angle in degrees (used only if euler and matrix are None).
    scale : 3-tuple or Vector
        Per-axis scale factors.
    euler : 3-tuple or Vector, optional
        Rotation expressed as Euler angles in radians (rx, ry, rz).
        If not None, this overrides axis/angle.
    euler_order : str, optional
        Euler rotation order (e.g. 'XYZ', 'ZXY', etc.). Used only when
        `euler` is not None.
    matrix : Matrix or 4×4 nested sequence, optional
        World-space 4×4 transform matrix. If provided, this is assigned
        directly to obj.matrix_world and all other transform parameters
        are ignored.

    Returns
    -------
    obj : bpy.types.Object
        The newly created Blender object.
    """

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Coerce parameters to Vectors (kept for backwards compatibility)

    loc_vec = Vector(loc)
    axis_vec = Vector(axis)
    if axis_vec.length == 0:
        axis_vec = Vector((0.0, 0.0, 1.0))
    else:
        axis_vec.normalize()

    scale_vec = Vector(scale)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Cube geometry in local space (size 2×2×2 centered at origin)

    verts = [
        Vector(( 1.0,  1.0, -1.0)),
        Vector(( 1.0, -1.0, -1.0)),
        Vector((-1.0, -1.0, -1.0)),
        Vector((-1.0,  1.0, -1.0)),
        Vector(( 1.0,  1.0,  1.0)),
        Vector(( 1.0, -1.0,  1.0)),
        Vector((-1.0, -1.0,  1.0)),
        Vector((-1.0,  1.0,  1.0)),
    ]

    faces = [
        (0, 1, 2, 3),
        (4, 7, 6, 5),
        (0, 4, 5, 1),
        (1, 5, 6, 2),
        (2, 6, 7, 3),
        (4, 0, 3, 7),
    ]

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Create mesh and object

    # If an object with this name already exists, remove it so we can recreate
    if name in bpy.data.objects:
        old_obj = bpy.data.objects[name]
        bpy.data.objects.remove(old_obj, do_unlink=True)

    mesh = bpy.data.meshes.new(name)
    mesh.from_pydata(verts, [], faces)
    mesh.update()

    obj = bpy.data.objects.new(name, mesh)
    bpy.context.scene.collection.objects.link(obj)

    bpy.context.view_layer.objects.active = obj
    obj.select_set(True)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Build world transform matrix and assign once

    # Highest priority: explicit world matrix
    if matrix is not None:
        # Accept either a mathutils.Matrix or any 4×4 sequence
        if isinstance(matrix, Matrix):
            M_world = matrix
        else:
            M_world = Matrix(matrix)

    else:
        # Translation
        T = Matrix.Translation(loc_vec)

        # Rotation from Euler angles (if provided)
        if euler is not None:
            from mathutils import Euler
            # Expect euler as (rx, ry, rz) in radians
            eul = Euler(euler, euler_order)
            R = eul.to_matrix().to_4x4()
        else:
            # Backwards-compatible axis + angle in degrees
            angle_rad = math.radians(angle)
            R = Matrix.Rotation(angle_rad, 4, axis_vec)

        # Scale
        S = Matrix.Diagonal((scale_vec.x, scale_vec.y, scale_vec.z, 1.0))

        # Combine: T * R * S (same as original order)
        M_world = T @ R @ S

    obj.matrix_world = M_world

    return obj

        M_world = T @ R @ S

    obj.matrix_world = M_world

    return obj

## Chapter 2 — Fabrication systems (overview)

1. **Pre-cut system** — oldest: timber cut/notched/drilled at factory, marked, bundled and assembled on site. More accurate than site cutting, minimal waste.
2. **Modular panel system** *(adopted in this manual, fig. 1)* — components built in factory by 2–3 men without cranes. Uniform wall panels sized on module M = 1.22 m (4 ft) to tally with Malaysian cladding sheets (plywood, hardboard, chipboard, cement board). Exploded view: floor joists → floor panels → wall panels → ceiling panels → roof truss.
3. **Large size panel system** (fig. 2) — panels up to 10–12 m (a dwelling length) factory-assembled; good for mass building many small houses; fewer site joints but higher transport/handling costs and cranes needed.
4. **Volume element system** (fig. 3) — dwellings completely finished at the factory on foundation beams; buyer sees the finished house beforehand; fastest site erection but needs trailers and cranes.

---

## Chapter 3 — Design of the house

- Traditional Malaysian construction is **post and beam** (beams 2–4 m apart on posts; non-load-bearing infill panels). The manual's house is instead **timber-framed (wood-framed)** — traditional in North America/Scandinavia, comparatively new in Malaysia.
- Two timber-frame methods:
  - **Balloon frame** (fig. 4): studs run full building height; intermediate floor joists side-fixed to studs. Only for 2–4 storey buildings.
  - **Platform frame** (fig. 5) — *used here*: shell built one storey at a time with storey-height wall panels; each floor becomes the construction platform for the next storey or roof.
- **Wall panel make-up** (fig. 6): top and bottom horizontal plates spaced for the designed height (2745 mm / 9 ft); vertical studs nailed between them at 610 mm centres (the text's "0.16 m centres" is a misprint — 610 mm everywhere else); noggings added to strengthen sheathing edges; sheets fixed one or both sides. All framework butt-jointed and nailed. Panels ≤3000 mm long for man-handling. Panels erected over the prepared platform, roof placed over to complete the building.
- **Advantages of timber-framed construction:** (1) simple transport of pre-assembled panels; (2) less site labour (more saved if factory-assembled); (3) panels erected manually by 2–3 men, no cranes; (4) speed — all wall panels of a house up in 2–3 days; once roofed, plumbing/electrical proceed in the dry; (5) low-cost high thermal insulation; (6) flexible design, modification and extension.

---

## Chapter 4 — Basic principles

- **Modular dimensioning:** best use of sheet materials + easy later extension. Local sheets are 1220 × 2440 mm, so planning uses multiples of **610 mm**; a 610 mm grid governs plan layout and positioning/fixing of partitions, roofs, joists (fig. 7).
- **Example plan (fig. 7):** proposed house 50 m² (7320 mm frontage × 5490 mm, with kitchen/WC/bath wing 4270 wide × 2440 deep at rear); future extension 3050 mm (bedroom 3) brings it to 63 m². Rooms: BR1, BR2, Living/Dining, Verandah, Kitchen, Bath, WC.
- **Load path (fig. 8):** unlike post-and-beam, the *wall panels are load-bearing*. Roof trusses (@1220 crs), studs (@610 crs) and floor joists (@610 crs) are kept **vertically in line** for efficient load transfer roof → studs → joists → ground. Section shows: roof truss / head binder / top plate / vertical stud / nogging / lintel / cripple stud / door / bottom plate / base plate / floor board / floor joist / bearer.
- **Load-bearing vs non-load-bearing walls (fig. 9):** load-bearing walls support floor/roof above. Non-load-bearing walls are partitions only — made **shorter** than load-bearing walls in the same storey so roof/floor joists above do not rest on them (clearance at top).
- **Openings:** doors/windows need a **lintel** spanning the opening, ends carried on **cripple studs** each side (fig. 8). Small openings need no lintel — simply framed between studs.
- **Panel-making tolerances:**
  1. Stud depth uniform throughout so finished panel-with-sheathing width is constant (e.g. for 47 × 97 studs, the 97 mm dimension must be accurate/regularised).
  2. 1–3 mm vertical gap between plywood sheathings for expansion, covered with beading.
  3. Finished length of each prefabricated panel 1–3 mm less than the drawing size.
- **Detached or linked houses:** houses may be linked by a **separating wall** (fig. 10; grid 305 mm, min 305 mm separating wall zone); empty space between neighbouring houses acts as a firebreak; minimum spacing per Uniform Building By-laws 1984.

### Sequence of construction (summary from Ch. 4)
- Main building at front on a raised platform **700 mm above ground**; kitchen at the back on ground-level concrete. Floor-to-ceiling **2745 mm (9 ft)**. Perspective in fig. 11.
- Order: concrete footings → posts on footings → bearers bolted across posts → floor joists with stiffening cross-pieces on bearers → T&G floor boards conceal-nailed → platform ready. Then pre-assembled wall panels erected over platform (kitchen, on ground level and not connected to the platform, can proceed simultaneously) → head binders/wall plates bind panel tops and support trusses → panels fixed sideways with nailed iron plates/angles, concealed with beading → prefabricated trussed rafter roofs on wall plates → rafters braced diagonally, purlins nailed → roofing sheets (now weathertight) → doors and windows → plumbing, wiring, sanitation → paint → occupy.

---

## Chapter 5 — General requirements and specification of materials

### Timber
- **Strength Group B** per Malaysian Standard M.S. 544:1978 (SIRIM).
- **Grade:** Standard structural grade per Malaysian Grading Rules (MGR) Part III Section J.
- **Sizes:** as drawings. Exposed surfaces planed; unexposed sawn unless regularised (e.g. the 97 mm of 47 × 97 studs must be fixed/accurate).
- **Moisture content at installation:** floor boards ≤ 18%; all other timber ≤ 22%.
- **Preservative treatment:** pressure impregnated with CCA to dry salt retention **5.6 kg/m³**, CCA penetration ≥ **12 mm**.

### Panels/boards
- **Plywood:** from a reputable mill; **WBP** (water-boil-proof) or **MR** (moisture-resistant) type per position in the plan.
- **Cement-bonded particleboard** (cemboard) for kitchen; fix per manufacturer's instructions.
- All other materials per good construction practice.

---

## Chapter 6 — Details of construction

### Site access
- Check/construct vehicle access, especially in remote areas. Electric power (mains or generator) and water (mains, well, river, or transported) still needed on site. Allocate storage space for prefabricated components away from the building area.

### Preparation of site
- Examine soil (timber house is light → most normal soils fine). If termite-infested, apply **anti-termite soil treatment before construction**.
- Clear vegetation, remove roots/cellulosic material during grading; ensure good drainage. Frontal (platform) part may sit on level ground or a gentle slope — level the platform by adjusting **footing level or post length** (fig. 12). Floor ≥ **700 mm above ground** for ventilation. Kitchen area at rear levelled by cut/fill with proper ramming.

### Setting out
- Don't build too close to the boundary (circulation; gap to neighbours acts as firebreak; min spacing per Uniform Building By-laws 1984). Locate near one end of a large plot to allow future extension (fig. 13).
- Drive temporary pegs at the four platform corners → set out with **batter boards**: 2 per corner (8 total), each of two vertical stakes **50 × 100 mm × ~1 m** driven ≥1 m beyond footing lines, with a horizontal board **25 × 150 mm** nailed on. All board tops levelled — surveyor's level or **transparent water-filled hose** (fig. 15); highest corner is the datum.
- Strings stretched between boards; positions marked with a nail or saw kerf so strings can be replaced. Two adjoining sides set with steel tapes; squareness checked with the diagonal — sides 7230 and 5400 mm → diagonal **√(7230² + 5400²) = 9096 mm** — or by the **3-4-5 rule** (fig. 16, plumb bob to a nail in a stake at the first corner). Fix three corners, establish the fourth, check both diagonals.
- Intermediate footing points marked with steel tape and plumb bob, always measuring from corners along the string. **All 12 footing positions set** (fig. 14: grid 3 × 2440 by 2 × 2700 centre lines of footings).

### Footings
- Remove strings, keep batter boards for later alignment/levelling.
- Excavate 12 holes **600 × 600 mm, 400 mm deep**; ram hardcore to **150 mm thick**; blind with a level of sand.
- Formwork for concrete; footing depth min **300 mm** (more on sloping contours if all footing tops are kept level; alternatively vary post lengths so footing tops need not be level). Footing top ≥ **50 mm above ground**.
- Before pouring: **12 mm MS bar reinforcement near the bottom**, **MS U-straps for posts set at the top**, aligned/levelled from batter-board strings and plumb bobs (fig. 12(i)).
- Concrete mix **1 : 2–3 : 4** (cement : sand : stone; sand per wetness), preferably machine-mixed (thorough hand mixing acceptable); pour and rod/vibrate to a dense concrete without disturbing reinforcement.

### Platform
- **Posts:** MS bearing plate **120 × 120 × 6 mm** placed inside the U-strap; posts **120 × 120 × 499 mm** dropped in; each fixed to the U-strap with **2 bolts** through predrilled holes (fig. 17).
- **Bearers:** one on each side of the post tops (**2/60 × 194**, i.e. paired), **4 bolts** through both bearers and post; washers under bolt heads/nuts bearing on timber. Lengthened with **splice pieces 2/25 × 194 × 300** between posts. Keep posts truly vertical and all bearer tops level and horizontal.
- **Joists:** 47 × 145 @ 610 crs on bearers, **slant-nailed with 75 mm nails**, one each side (fig. 18). Stiffening cross-pieces against tilting: **50 × 50 at each end**, **50 × 75 at the centre**, seated in notches cut in the joist tops (fig. 19).
- **Floor boards:** T&G strip flooring laid across joists (Ch. 6 text: 30 × 145; Table 1/drawings: 22 × 145); fit groove over tongue snugly and **blind-nail through the tongue at 40–50°** into the joist (fig. 20). **Header joist 20 × 194** nailed to joist ends, top level with the floor boards, concealing the joist spaces (fig. 21).
- Platform complete → kitchen construction can start separately or simultaneously.

### Wall panels
- Panels pre-assembled at the factory (more accurate) or on site (pre-cut pieces save labour; assemble on a level surface such as a concrete slab or trestles).
- **Base/sill plates** fixed over the platform first: **47 × 112 (exterior)**, **47 × 84 (interior)** to match panel widths (fig. 22 shows base plate layout with joints). Check positions and corner squareness, then nail to floor boards with **76 mm nails @ 300 mm centres in a zigzag** pattern.
- **Erection (fig. 23):** first panel is corner panel No. 1; skew-nail its bottom to the base plate; hold upright with **temporary diagonal braces** (removed only when panels are permanently fixed). Then subsequent panels. **21 panels over the platform, 6 over the kitchen.**
- Panels **2745 mm high**, longest **2550 mm** → man-handled without cranes. Four **temporary lifting handles** fixed ~1000 mm high near the ends of each double-sheathed panel; removed once in position.
- **Wall plates/head binders** over panel tops: **47 × 112** on thicker exterior walls, **22 × 84** on thinner interior walls (thin 22 mm plates keep the tops of non-load-bearing walls clear of trusses). Nailed with 76 mm nails @ 300 crs zigzag.
- **Panel-to-base-plate fixing:** **Pryda knuckle nail plates 2N10** (89 mm wide × 63 mm deep, 2 rows of 10 punched-out nails) or similar @ **610 mm centres on the exterior side**; interior side skew-nailed with 76 mm nails to the base plate. Metal plates and nails covered by **plywood skirting 9 × 100 mm**.
- **Panel-to-panel (side) fixing:** 3 Pryda 2N10 plates, evenly spaced. **Corner (right-angle) fixing:** 3 **Pryda angle plates 3NA** (44 × 44 × 95) on the interior angle. All plates covered with **plywood beading** (2/9 × 72; fig. 24: length-wise panels and corner panels, nail plates 63 × 89 @ 610 spacing).
- Erect **kitchen walls before roof trusses** — the extended trusses of the main building rest on the rear kitchen wall.

### Kitchen
- Area ~**3.1 × 5.1 m** behind the main building. Excavate to level; hardcore rammed to **100 mm**; blind top with sand and wet liberally; pour **100 mm concrete floor, mix 1:2:4**. **Strip footings 150 wide × 50 thick** additionally under wall-panel lines (fig. 25 drawing labels: conc. curb 50 × 115 for wall panels; conc. floor 100 mm; strip footing 200 × 100; slab 2443 × 4500).
- **Concrete curbs replace timber sole plates** (wet nature of the kitchen): **50 mm thick × 115 mm wide** for thicker walls, **50 × 84** for thinner. **Bolts 12 × 100 mm** cast vertically into the curbs, 38 mm embedded, threads exposed; ~**2 bolts per panel** (fig. 26: anchor bolt @ 1 m crs).
- Kitchen panels sheathed both sides with **cement-bonded particleboard: 10 mm outside, 8 mm inside**. Pre-assembly covers only the 10 mm side; **elongated holes** drilled in the bottom rail to match curb bolts; panel dropped over bolts and tightened with nut and washer; 8 mm inside sheet fixed in situ (predrill nail holes in cemboard).
- Wall plates on top; side/corner attachments with Pryda (or equivalent) plates as for plywood panels.

### Roof trusses
- Trussed rafters preferably factory pre-assembled. Joints: **nailed 9 mm WBP plywood gusset plates both sides** (per plan) or **proprietary punched metal plates** (then fabricated by the licensed factory which also sizes the plates; timber member sizes unchanged). All members **35 × 72 mm**.
- **Erection:** first truss at one end, nailed to wall plate, **temporarily braced to the ground at two places with 50 × 100 timber** (fig. 27) — must be firm, all other trusses fasten back to it. Second truss placed **upside down** with ends on opposite wall plates, peak hanging down, then **tilted up with a long "Y"-ended pole** (fig. 28); nail to wall plate, brace to first truss; repeat. Attachment: **skew-nailed 4/100 mm nails per truss-to-plate joint, two each side** (fig. 29).
- **Gable ends** (platform area): closed with **6 mm plywood** cut to size; roof-space **ventilation through holes drilled in these gable sheets**.
- **Kitchen end:** four trusses have **extended rafters** covering the kitchen, resting on the kitchen wall plate; **two additional 35 × 72 beams between each pair of trusses** stiffen the kitchen roof.
- Manual erection by **4 workers** (one on each wall nailing, one at truss centre fixing the top, one general/lifting); crane faster if available.
- **Permanent bracing** against wind sway: horizontal braces at right angles to trusses; **diagonal braces at 45°** from top of the gable-end truss to the bottom of the fourth truss (fig. 30; braces 22 × 97). Then remove temporary bracing.
- **Purlins 35 × 72** on top of trusses, skew-nailed to each rafter with **two 76 mm nails**, one per side (fig. 31). Fascia and barge boards fixed to rafter/purlin ends.
- **Roofing:** corrugated **asbestos-free fibre cement sheets** laid over purlins per manufacturer's instructions. Building now dry regardless of weather.

### Doors and windows
- Openings pre-formed in wall panels. Door openings keep a **full-length bottom rail** during handling (prevents twisting); after erection the exposed rail portion is **cut out together with the base plate** at the opening (fig. 32).
- Doors/windows factory-assembled, delivered for installation. **Door sizes: 700 (WC/bath), 770 (kitchen/rooms), 840 (main entrance); all 2100 mm high** from floor level. Door/window dimensions must match panel openings exactly. **All doors open inwards.**
- **Flush doors:** framework assembled square, plywood glued and nailed both sides.
- **Windows:** frames made on site in the panel openings. **Adjustable aluminium louvre frames with 8 leaves** fixed to the wooden window frame; glass sheets cut to size slide into the louvre slots; glass sheets also used as **fixed glass louvres** above the adjustable ones.

### Railings and stairs
- **Railings:** rails 47 × 97, vertical balustrades 20 × 20; rail top at **1000 mm above floor**.
- **Stairs (2 off — entrance & kitchen):** rise **170 mm**, run **230 mm**. Treads **47 × 250** rest both ends on ledgers **50 × 50 × 180** fixed to stringers **60 × 219**. Stringers lean against the floor joist at the top and fix to the concrete landing with **angle-iron plates 63 × 63 × 200** at the bottom (fig. 33).

### Ceiling
- **Noggings 38 × 50 @ 610 crs** fixed between roof trusses first (fig. 34). Ceiling of **6 mm plywood or 6 mm cement-bonded particleboard** (Table 1 lists 4 mm MR plywood 2' × 8'), nailed to noggings and trussed rafters **in a zigzag pattern**. Ceiling in the **main building only**, not the kitchen.

### Services
- Plumbing/electrical/sewerage can start as soon as roofing sheets are on.
- **Wiring holes:** 25 mm diameter drilled at the **centre of the section** of wall frames and floor joists; ≥ **300 mm from ends** of studs/joists and from any other hole (fig. 35: electric socket fixed to 50 × 50 blocking).
- **Notches in joists** allowed only if: (1) in the **top edge**; (2) located **1/10–1/5 of the span from the support**; (3) depth ≤ **21 mm for a 145 mm joist**. Otherwise drill holes for piping (fig. 36: holes 300–550 mm from support, centred with 50/25/50 spacing on a 145 joist).
- Fixtures fix to the panel framing timbers; add extra noggings for heavy fixtures (wash basins, boilers).

### Finishing touches
- **Plywood skirtings 9 × 100 mm** between wall and floor (main building); **plywood beadings 9 × 72 mm** cover all plywood joints.
- Paint the whole building (protection, cleaning, appearance — unfinished exposed wood weathers quickly). Floors: natural colour/grain attractive; apply floor finish against wear/abrasion. Building ready for occupation.

---

## Chapter 7 — Maintenance and repair

Two enemies of the tropical timber house: **termite attack** and **moisture/damp decay**.

**Raised platform:** keep underfloor space well ventilated (no blocking by grasses/shrubs/stored items); no standing water under the building — soil grades away from the house; keep tops of all concrete (footings, stair landing, kitchen floor) **50–100 mm above ground** as designed; inspect regularly for termite activity — **break earthen termite tunnels** (subterranean termites need soil-to-building contact); treat soil with insecticide if possible.

**Exterior walls:** no part should collect water (moisture → fungi, decay — common on door/window frames); seal shrinkage/workmanship cracks with putty; rust spots at exposed non-corrosive nail heads — set heads below surface and putty over; repaint deteriorated finishes.

**Interior:** fill cracks with putty and paint; don't let moisture linger on timber/plywood (especially kitchen); sheathing damage — small holes puttied and sanded, larger holes cut out and a new section fitted; floor-board shrinkage gaps (boards laid at high MC) — glue matching timber strips into gaps, or replace floor sections in severe cases.

**Roof:** ceiling stains indicate leaks — locate and repair; maintain roof-space air circulation — keep gable-end ventilation openings provided and unblocked.

---

## References

- *Uniform Building By-Law 1984*. MDC Sdn. Bhd.
- *Code of Practice for the Structural Use of Timber*, Malaysian Standard M.S. 544:1978 (SIRIM).
- *The Malaysian Grading Rules for Sawn Hardwood Timber (MGR)*, Malaysian Timber Industry Board, 1984.

---

## Appendix I — Detailed technical drawings (9 sheets, key data)

**Sheet: Plan, elevations, sections, floor joist layout**
- Front/side elevations: platform 700 mm above ground; overall height to eaves ~2869 mm; louvre windows; verandah with railing and entrance stair.
- Plan on 610 mm grid: main block 7320 × 5490 (BR1, BR2, L/D, VER) + rear wing 4270 wide (KIT, B, W.C).
- Floor joist layout: overall 7544 × 5714; posts 120 × 120 on conc. footings 600 × 600; bearers 2/60 × 194 spliced 2/10 × 194 × 440 joined with 4 bolts; floor joists 47 × 145 @ 610 crs; strip floor 22 × 145 T&G. Section A-A footing bays 2440/2440/2440 (spans 4500 + 3044); Section B-B bays 2700/2700.

**Sheet: Panel layout plan (Drg 101/94/2 of 9)**
- All **27 panels numbered** ①–㉗ around the plan: platform panels 1–21, kitchen panels 22–27 (22 kitchen wall 1845/2555; 25 = 1220 W.C. panel etc.). Details X/Y: 6 mm plywood filler pieces at wall junctions.

**Sheet: Sections A-A and B-B through house**
- Truss over platform with extended rafter over kitchen; water tank (750 × 1220 × 540) on 4/47 × 97 beams above bath; purlins 35 × 72; wall heights 2745 (platform), kitchen lower; stairs: tread 47 × 250 on 50 × 50 × 180, stringer 60 × 219, platform 700 above ground; ceiling heights 2440 (kitchen zone) noted; wire mesh above kitchen wall to seal gap to roof.

**Sheets: Panel elevations and plan views (panels 1–27)**
- Each panel drawn with 6 mm plywood side elevation, 9 mm plywood side elevation, and horizontal plan section; stud positions on 610/1220 spacings; window/door openings with lintels and cripple studs; some panels have VOID zones over exposed columns; filler pieces where panels meet columns.
- **Summary of wall panels table:**

| Panels | Studs | External sheathing | Internal sheathing |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1–17 | 47 × 97 | Plywood 9 mm (WBP) | Plywood 6 mm (MR) |
| 18–21 | 47 × 72 | Plywood 6 mm | Plywood 6 mm |
| 22–24, 26–27 | 47 × 97 | Cemboard 10 mm | Cemboard 8 mm |
| 25 | 47 × 72 | Cemboard 8 mm | Cemboard 8 mm |

- Sheathing size tolerance ±4 mm to allow expansion gap between sheathings.

**Sheet: Door/window details & panel types (Drg 101/94/6 of 9)**
- Window (1220 wide × 1587 in 2440 panel, sill at 900 FL): lintel 97 × 145; frame ex 47 × 112; fixed glass louvres @ 90°, beading 12 × 12; Naco louvres 8 leaves with security bars; sill ex 47 × 145.
- Door (840 × 2100): lintel 97 × 145, cripple studs 47 × 97, bottom rail cut off after erection; stopper 12 × 40; studs 25 × 100 / 25 × 75 in d

2	# Construction Manual of Prefabricated Timber House — Extracted Notes
3	
4	**Source:** *Construction Manual of Prefabricated Timber House*, FRIM Technical Information Handbook No. 5, by Mohd Shukari Midon, Chu Yue Pun, Hilmi Md Tahir, Nor Azian Mohd Kasby. Forest Research Institute Malaysia (FRIM) / International Tropical Timber Organization (ITTO), 1996. ISBN 983-9592-55-6. Produced under the project "Research on the Utilization of Tropical Timber in Construction". Extracted from `Construction Manual Of Prefabricated Timber House.pdf`.
5	
6	**Scope:** Step-by-step construction of a prefabricated 'low-cost' single-storey timber-framed house (platform frame method, **Modular Panel System**) designed for Malaysia/tropical climates (not suitable for very strong winds or hurricanes). Panels may be factory-made or assembled on site DIY-style. Internal partitions are non-load-bearing and can be rearranged without affecting structural strength. Appendix contains 9 sheets of detailed technical drawings.
7	
8	---
9	
10	## Key dimensions quick reference
11	
12	| Parameter | Value |
13	|---|---|
14	| Module 'M' | 1.22 m (4 ft) — matches local sheet materials |
15	| Planning grid | 610 mm (dimensions are multiples of 610 mm) |
16	| Sheet material size | 1220 × 2440 mm (printed "1220 x 2240", evidently a typo) |

21	| Max panel length | ≤3000 mm for man-handling (longest actual panel 2550 mm) |
22	| Platform height above ground | 700 mm minimum (ventilation) |
23	| Built-up area | 50 m² proposed house; 63 m² with future extension |

25	| Number of wall panels | 21 over platform + 6 over kitchen = 27 total |
26	| Footings | 12 concrete footings; hole 600 × 600 × 400 mm deep |
27	| Posts | 120 × 120 × 499 mm high timber on concrete footings |
28	| Studs | 47 × 97 mm (thicker/exterior panels), 47 × 72 mm (thinner/interior) |
29	| Floor joists | 47 × 145 mm @ 610 crs |
30	| Bearers | double 60 × 197 mm (2 per post row; drawings label 2/60 × 194) |

40	| House height | ~2869 mm to eaves over 700 mm platform (side elevation) |
41	
42	---
43	
44	## Chapter 2 — Fabrication systems (overview)
45	
46	1. **Pre-cut system** — oldest: timber cut/notched/drilled at factory, marked, bundled and assembled on site. More accurate than site cutting, minimal waste.
47	2. **Modular panel system** *(adopted in this manual, fig. 1)* — components built in factory by 2–3 men without cranes. Uniform wall panels sized on module M = 1.22 m (4 ft) to tally with Malaysian cladding sheets (plywood, hardboard, chipboard, cement board). Exploded view: floor joists → floor panels → wall panels → ceiling panels → roof truss.
48	3. **Large size panel system** (fig. 2) — panels up to 10–12 m (a dwelling length) factory-assembled; good for mass building many small houses; fewer site joints but higher transport/handling costs and cranes needed.
49	4. **Volume element system** (fig. 3) — dwellings completely finished at the factory on foundation beams; buyer sees the finished house beforehand; fastest site erection but needs trailers and cranes.
50	
51	---
52	
53	## Chapter 3 — Design of the house
54	
55	- Traditional Malaysian construction is **post and beam** (beams 2–4 m apart on posts; non-load-bearing infill panels). The manual's house is instead **timber-framed (wood-framed)** — traditional in North America/Scandinavia, comparatively new in Malaysia.
56	- Two timber-frame methods:
57	  - **Balloon frame** (fig. 4): studs run full building height; intermediate floor joists side-fixed to studs. Only for 2–4 storey buildings.
58	  - **Platform frame** (fig. 5) — *used here*: shell built one storey at a time with storey-height wall panels; each floor becomes the construction platform for the next storey or roof.
59	- **Wall panel make-up** (fig. 6): top and bottom horizontal plates spaced for the designed height (2745 mm / 9 ft); vertical studs nailed between them at 610 mm centres (the text's "0.16 m centres" is a misprint — 610 mm everywhere else); noggings added to strengthen sheathing edges; sheets fixed one or both sides. All framework butt-jointed and nailed. Panels ≤3000 mm long for man-handling. Panels erected over the prepared platform, roof placed over to complete the building.
60	- **Advantages of timber-framed construction:** (1) simple transport of pre-assembled panels; (2) less site labour (more saved if factory-assembled); (3) panels erected manually by 2–3 men, no cranes; (4) speed — all wall panels of a house up in 2–3 days; once roofed, plumbing/electrical proceed in the dry; (5) low-cost high thermal insulation; (6) flexible design, modification and extension.
61	
62	---
63	
64	## Chapter 4 — Basic principles
65	
66	- **Modular dimensioning:** best use of sheet materials + easy later extension. Local sheets are 1220 × 2440 mm, so planning uses multiples of **610 mm**; a 610 mm grid governs plan layout and positioning/fixing of partitions, roofs, joists (fig. 7).
67	- **Example plan (fig. 7):** proposed house 50 m² (7320 mm frontage × 5490 mm, with kitchen/WC/bath wing 4270 wide × 2440 deep at rear); future extension 3050 mm (bedroom 3) brings it to 63 m². Rooms: BR1, BR2, Living/Dining, Verandah, Kitchen, Bath, WC.
68	- **Load path (fig. 8):** unlike post-and-beam, the *wall panels are load-bearing*. Roof trusses (@1220 crs), studs (@610 crs) and floor joists (@610 crs) are kept **vertically in line** for efficient load transfer roof → studs → joists → ground. Section shows: roof truss / head binder / top plate / vertical stud / nogging / lintel / cripple stud / door / bottom plate / base plate / floor board / floor joist / bearer.
69	- **Load-bearing vs non-load-bearing walls (fig. 9):** load-bearing walls support floor/roof above. Non-load-bearing walls are partitions only — made **shorter** than load-bearing walls in the same storey so roof/floor joists above do not rest on them (clearance at top).
70	- **Openings:** doors/windows need a **lintel** spanning the opening, ends carried on **cripple studs** each side (fig. 8). Small openings need no lintel — simply framed between studs.
71	- **Panel-making tolerances:**
72	  1. Stud depth uniform throughout so finished panel-with-sheathing width is constant (e.g. for 47 × 97 studs, the 97 mm dimension must be accurate/regularised).
73	  2. 1–3 mm vertical gap between plywood sheathings for expansion, covered with beading.
74	  3. Finished length of each prefabricated panel 1–3 mm less than the drawing size.
75	- **Detached or linked houses:** houses may be linked by a **separating wall** (fig. 10; grid 305 mm, min 305 mm separating wall zone); empty space between neighbouring houses acts as a firebreak; minimum spacing per Uniform Building By-laws 1984.
76	
77	### Sequence of construction (summary from Ch. 4)
78	- Main building at front on a raised platform **700 mm above ground**; kitchen at the back on ground-level concrete. Floor-to-ceiling **2745 mm (9 ft)**. Perspective in fig. 11.
79	- Order: concrete footings → posts on footings → bearers bolted across posts → floor joists with stiffening cross-pieces on bearers → T&G floor boards conceal-nailed → platform ready. Then pre-assembled wall panels erected over platform (kitchen, on ground level and not connected to the platform, can proceed simultaneously) → head binders/wall plates bind panel tops and support trusses → panels fixed sideways with nailed iron plates/angles, concealed with beading → prefabricated trussed rafter roofs on wall plates → rafters braced diagonally, purlins nailed → roofing sheets (now weathertight) → doors and windows → plumbing, wiring, sanitation → paint → occupy.

188	
189	## Chapter 6 — Details of construction
190	
191	### Site access
192	- Check/construct vehicle access, especially in remote areas. Electric power (mains or generator) and water (mains, well, river, or transported) still needed on site. Allocate storage space for prefabricated components away from the building area.
193	
194	### Preparation of site
195	- Examine soil (timber house is light → most normal soils fine). If termite-infested, apply **anti-termite soil treatment before construction**.
196	- Clear vegetation, remove roots/cellulosic material during grading; ensure good drainage. Frontal (platform) part may sit on level ground or a gentle slope — level the platform by adjusting **footing level or post length** (fig. 12). Floor ≥ **700 mm above ground** for ventilation. Kitchen area at rear levelled by cut/fill with proper ramming.
197	
198	### Setting out
199	- Don't build too close to the boundary (circulation; gap to neighbours acts as firebreak; min spacing per Uniform Building By-laws 1984). Locate near one end of a large plot to allow future extension (fig. 13).
200	- Drive temporary pegs at the four platform corners → set out with **batter boards**: 2 per corner (8 total), each of two vertical stakes **50 × 100 mm × ~1 m** driven ≥1 m beyond footing lines, with a horizontal board **25 × 150 mm** nailed on. All board tops levelled — surveyor's level or **transparent water-filled hose** (fig. 15); highest corner is the datum.
201	- Strings stretched between boards; positions marked with a nail or saw kerf so strings can be replaced. Two adjoining sides set with steel tapes; squareness checked with the diagonal — sides 7230 and 5400 mm → diagonal **√(7230² + 5400²) = 9096 mm** — or by the **3-4-5 rule** (fig. 16, plumb bob to a nail in a stake at the first corner). Fix three corners, establish the fourth, check both diagonals.
202	- Intermediate footing points marked with steel tape and plumb bob, always measuring from corners along the string. **All 12 footing positions set** (fig. 14: grid 3 × 2440 by 2 × 2700 centre lines of footings).
203	
204	### Footings
205	- Remove strings, keep batter boards for later alignment/levelling.
206	- Excavate 12 holes **600 × 600 mm, 400 mm deep**; ram hardcore to **150 mm thick**; blind with a level of sand.
207	- Formwork for concrete; footing depth min **300 mm** (more on sloping contours if all footing tops are kept level; alternatively vary post lengths so footing tops need not be level). Footing top ≥ **50 mm above ground**.
208	- Before pouring: **12 mm MS bar reinforcement near the bottom**, **MS U-straps for posts set at the top**, aligned/levelled from batter-board strings and plumb bobs (fig. 12(i)).
209	- Concrete mix **1 : 2–3 : 4** (cement : sand : stone; sand per wetness), preferably machine-mixed (thorough hand mixing acceptable); pour and rod/vibrate to a dense concrete without disturbing reinforcement.
210	
211	### Platform
212	- **Posts:** MS bearing plate **120 × 120 × 6 mm** placed inside the U-strap; posts **120 × 120 × 499 mm** dropped in; each fixed to the U-strap with **2 bolts** through predrilled holes (fig. 17).
213	- **Bearers:** one on each side of the post tops (**2/60 × 194**, i.e. paired), **4 bolts** through both bearers and post; washers under bolt heads/nuts bearing on timber. Lengthened with **splice pieces 2/25 × 194 × 300** between posts. Keep posts truly vertical and all bearer tops level and horizontal.
214	- **Joists:** 47 × 145 @ 610 crs on bearers, **slant-nailed with 75 mm nails**, one each side (fig. 18). Stiffening cross-pieces against tilting: **50 × 50 at each end**, **50 × 75 at the centre**, seated in notches cut in the joist tops (fig. 19).
215	- **Floor boards:** T&G strip flooring laid across joists (Ch. 6 text: 30 × 145; Table 1/drawings: 22 × 145); fit groove over tongue snugly and **blind-nail through the tongue at 40–50°** into the joist (fig. 20). **Header joist 20 × 194** nailed to joist ends, top level with the floor boards, concealing the joist spaces (fig. 21).
216	- Platform complete → kitchen construction can start separately or simultaneously.
217	
218	### Wall panels
219	- Panels pre-assembled at the factory (more accurate) or on site (pre-cut pieces save labour; assemble on a level surface such as a concrete slab or trestles).
220	- **Base/sill plates** fixed over the platform first: **47 × 112 (exterior)**, **47 × 84 (interior)** to match panel widths (fig. 22 shows base plate layout with joints). Check positions and corner squareness, then nail to floor boards with **76 mm nails @ 300 mm centres in a zigzag** pattern.
221	- **Erection (fig. 23):** first panel is corner panel No. 1; skew-nail its bottom to the base plate; hold upright with **temporary diagonal braces** (removed only when panels are permanently fixed). Then subsequent panels. **21 panels over the platform, 6 over the kitchen.**
222	- Panels **2745 mm high**, longest **2550 mm** → man-handled without cranes. Four **temporary lifting handles** fixed ~1000 mm high near the ends of each double-sheathed panel; removed once in position.
223	- **Wall plates/head binders** over panel tops: **47 × 112** on thicker exterior walls, **22 × 84** on thinner interior walls (thin 22 mm plates keep the tops of non-load-bearing walls clear of trusses). Nailed with 76 mm nails @ 300 crs zigzag.
224	- **Panel-to-base-plate fixing:** **Pryda knuckle nail plates 2N10** (89 mm wide × 63 mm deep, 2 rows of 10 punched-out nails) or similar @ **610 mm centres on the exterior side**; interior side skew-nailed with 76 mm nails to the base plate. Metal plates and nails covered by **plywood skirting 9 × 100 mm**.
225	- **Panel-to-panel (side) fixing:** 3 Pryda 2N10 plates, evenly spaced. **Corner (right-angle) fixing:** 3 **Pryda angle plates 3NA** (44 × 44 × 95) on the interior angle. All plates covered with **plywood beading** (2/9 × 72; fig. 24: length-wise panels and corner panels, nail plates 63 × 89 @ 610 spacing).
226	- Erect **kitchen walls before roof trusses** — the extended trusses of the main building rest on the rear kitchen wall.
227	
228	### Kitchen
229	- Area ~**3.1 × 5.1 m** behind the main building. Excavate to level; hardcore rammed to **100 mm**; blind top with sand and wet liberally; pour **100 mm concrete floor, mix 1:2:4**. **Strip footings 150 wide × 50 thick** additionally under wall-panel lines (fig. 25 drawing labels: conc. curb 50 × 115 for wall panels; conc. floor 100 mm; strip footing 200 × 100; slab 2443 × 4500).
230	- **Concrete curbs replace timber sole plates** (wet nature of the kitchen): **50 mm thick × 115 mm wide** for thicker walls, **50 × 84** for thinner. **Bolts 12 × 100 mm** cast vertically into the curbs, 38 mm embedded, threads exposed; ~**2 bolts per panel** (fig. 26: anchor bolt @ 1 m crs).
231	- Kitchen panels sheathed both sides with **cement-bonded particleboard: 10 mm outside, 8 mm inside**. Pre-assembly covers only the 10 mm side; **elongated holes** drilled in the bottom rail to match curb bolts; panel dropped over bolts and tightened with nut and washer; 8 mm inside sheet fixed in situ (predrill nail holes in cemboard).
232	- Wall plates on top; side/corner attachments with Pryda (or equivalent) plates as for plywood panels.
233	
234	### Roof trusses
235	- Trussed rafters preferably factory pre-assembled. Joints: **nailed 9 mm WBP plywood gusset plates both sides** (per plan) or **proprietary punched metal plates** (then fabricated by the licensed factory which also sizes the plates; timber member sizes unchanged). All members **35 × 72 mm**.
236	- **Erection:** first truss at one end, nailed to wall plate, **temporarily braced to the ground at two places with 50 × 100 timber** (fig. 27) — must be firm, all other trusses fasten back to it. Second truss placed **upside down** with ends on opposite wall plates, peak hanging down, then **tilted up with a long "Y"-ended pole** (fig. 28); nail to wall plate, brace to first truss; repeat. Attachment: **skew-nailed 4/100 mm nails per truss-to-plate joint, two each side** (fig. 29).
237	- **Gable ends** (platform area): closed with **6 mm plywood** cut to size; roof-space **ventilation through holes drilled in these gable sheets**.
238	- **Kitchen end:** four trusses have **extended rafters** covering the kitchen, resting on the kitchen wall plate; **two additional 35 × 72 beams between each pair of trusses** stiffen the kitchen roof.
239	- Manual erection by **4 workers** (one on each wall nailing, one at truss centre fixing the top, one general/lifting); crane faster if available.
240	- **Permanent bracing** against wind sway: horizontal braces at right angles to trusses; **diagonal braces at 45°** from top of the gable-end truss to the bottom of the fourth truss (fig. 30; braces 22 × 97). Then remove temporary bracing.
241	- **Purlins 35 × 72** on top of trusses, skew-nailed to each rafter with **two 76 mm nails**, one per side (fig. 31). Fascia and barge boards fixed to rafter/purlin ends.
242	- **Roofing:** corrugated **asbestos-free fibre cement sheets** laid over purlins per manufacturer's instructions. Building now dry regardless of weather.
243	
244	### Doors and windows
245	- Openings pre-formed in wall panels. Door openings keep a **full-length bottom rail** during handling (prevents twisting); after erection the exposed rail portion is **cut out together with the base plate** at the opening (fig. 32).
246	- Doors/windows factory-assembled, delivered for installation. **Door sizes: 700 (WC/bath), 770 (kitchen/rooms), 840 (main entrance); all 2100 mm high** from floor level. Door/window dimensions must match panel openings exactly. **All doors open inwards.**
247	- **Flush doors:** framework assembled square, plywood glued and nailed both sides.
248	- **Windows:** frames made on site in the panel openings. **Adjustable aluminium louvre frames with 8 leaves** fixed to the wooden window frame; glass sheets cut to size slide into the louvre slots; glass sheets also used as **fixed glass louvres** above the adjustable ones.
249	
250	### Railings and stairs
251	- **Railings:** rails 47 × 97, vertical balustrades 20 × 20; rail top at **1000 mm above floor**.
252	- **Stairs (2 off — entrance & kitchen):** rise **170 mm**, run **230 mm**. Treads **47 × 250** rest both ends on ledgers **50 × 50 × 180** fixed to stringers **60 × 219**. Stringers lean against the floor joist at the top and fix to the concrete landing with **angle-iron plates 63 × 63 × 200** at the bottom (fig. 33).
253	
254	### Ceiling
255	- **Noggings 38 × 50 @ 610 crs** fixed between roof trusses first (fig. 34). Ceiling of **6 mm plywood or 6 mm cement-bonded particleboard** (Table 1 lists 4 mm MR plywood 2' × 8'), nailed to noggings and trussed rafters **in a zigzag pattern**. Ceiling in the **main building only**, not the kitchen.
256	
257	### Services
258	- Plumbing/electrical/sewerage can start as soon as roofing sheets are on.
259	- **Wiring holes:** 25 mm diameter drilled at the **centre of the section** of wall frames and floor joists; ≥ **300 mm from ends** of studs/joists and from any other hole (fig. 35: electric socket fixed to 50 × 50 blocking).
260	- **Notches in joists** allowed only if: (1) in the **top edge**; (2) located **1/10–1/5 of the span from the support**; (3) depth ≤ **21 mm for a 145 mm joist**. Otherwise drill holes for piping (fig. 36: holes 300–550 mm from support, centred with 50/25/50 spacing on a 145 joist).
261	- Fixtures fix to the panel framing timbers; add extra noggings for heavy fixtures (wash basins, boilers).
262	
263	### Finishing touches
264	- **Plywood skirtings 9 × 100 mm** between wall and floor (main building); **plywood beadings 9 × 72 mm** cover all plywood joints.
265	- Paint the whole building (protection, cleaning, appearance — unfinished exposed wood weathers quickly). Floors: natural colour/grain attractive; apply floor finish against wear/abrasion. Building ready for occupation.
266	
267	---
268	
269	## Chapter 7 — Maintenance and repair
270	
271	Two enemies of the tropical timber house: **termite attack** and **moisture/damp decay**.
272	
273	**Raised platform:** keep underfloor space well ventilated (no blocking by grasses/shrubs/stored items); no standing water under the building — soil grades away from the house; keep tops of all concrete (footings, stair landing, kitchen floor) **50–100 mm above ground** as designed; inspect regularly for termite activity — **break earthen termite tunnels** (subterranean termites need soil-to-building contact); treat soil with insecticide if possible.
274	
275	**Exterior walls:** no part should collect water (moisture → fungi, decay — common on door/window frames); seal shrinkage/workmanship cracks with putty; rust spots at exposed non-corrosive nail heads — set heads below surface and putty over; repaint deteriorated finishes.
276	
277	**Interior:** fill cracks with putty and paint; don't let moisture linger on timber/plywood (especially kitchen); sheathing damage — small holes puttied and sanded, larger holes cut out and a new section fitted; floor-board shrinkage gaps (boards laid at high MC) — glue matching timber strips into gaps, or replace floor sections in severe cases.
278	
279	**Roof:** ceiling stains indicate leaks — locate and repair; maintain roof-space air circulation — keep gable-end ventilation openings provided and unblocked.
280	
281	---
282	
283	## References
284	
285	- *Uniform Building By-Law 1984*. MDC Sdn. Bhd.
286	- *Code of Practice for the Structural Use of Timber*, Malaysian Standard M.S. 544:1978 (SIRIM).
287	- *The Malaysian Grading Rules for Sawn Hardwood Timber (MGR)*, Malaysian Timber Industry Board, 1984.
288	
289	---
290	
291	## Appendix I — Detailed technical drawings (9 sheets, key data)
292	
293	**Sheet: Plan, elevations, sections, floor joist layout**
294	- Front/side elevations: platform 700 mm above ground; overall height to eaves ~2869 mm; louvre windows; verandah with railing and entrance stair.
295	- Plan on 610 mm grid: main block 7320 × 5490 (BR1, BR2, L/D, VER) + rear wing 4270 wide (KIT, B, W.C).
296	- Floor joist layout: overall 7544 × 5714; posts 120 × 120 on conc. footings 600 × 600; bearers 2/60 × 194 spliced 2/10 × 194 × 440 joined with 4 bolts; floor joists 47 × 145 @ 610 crs; strip floor 22 × 145 T&G. Section A-A footing bays 2440/2440/2440 (spans 4500 + 3044); Section B-B bays 2700/2700.
297	
298	**Sheet: Panel layout plan (Drg 101/94/2 of 9)**
299	- All **27 panels numbered** ①–㉗ around the plan: platform panels 1–21, kitchen panels 22–27 (22 kitchen wall 1845/2555; 25 = 1220 W.C. panel etc.). Details X/Y: 6 mm plywood filler pieces at wall junctions.
300	
301	**Sheet: Sections A-A and B-B through house**
302	- Truss over platform with extended rafter over kitchen; water tank (750 × 1220 × 540) on 4/47 × 97 beams above bath; purlins 35 × 72; wall heights 2745 (platform), kitchen lower; stairs: tread 47 × 250 on 50 × 50 × 180, stringer 60 × 219, platform 700 above ground; ceiling heights 2440 (kitchen zone) noted; wire mesh above kitchen wall to seal gap to roof.
303	
304	**Sheets: Panel elevations and plan views (panels 1–27)**
305	- Each panel drawn with 6 mm plywood side elevation, 9 mm plywood side elevation, and horizontal plan section; stud positions on 610/1220 spacings; window/door openings with lintels and cripple studs; some panels have VOID zones over exposed columns; filler pieces where panels meet columns.
306	- **Summary of wall panels table:**
307	
308	| Panels | Studs | External sheathing | Internal sheathing |
309	|---|---|---|---|
310	| 1–17 | 47 × 97 | Plywood 9 mm (WBP) | Plywood 6 mm (MR) |
311	| 18–21 | 47 × 72 | Plywood 6 mm | Plywood 6 mm |
312	| 22–24, 26–27 | 47 × 97 | Cemboard 10 mm | Cemboard 8 mm |
313	| 25 | 47 × 72 | Cemboard 8 mm | Cemboard 8 mm |
314	
315	- Sheathing size tolerance ±4 mm to allow expansion gap between sheathings.
316	
317	**Sheet: Door/window details & panel types (Drg 101/94/6 of 9)**
318	- Window (1220 wide × 1587 in 2440 panel, sill at 900 FL): lintel 97 × 145; frame ex 47 × 112; fixed glass louvres @ 90°, beading 12 × 12; Naco louvres 8 leaves with security bars; sill ex 47 × 145.
319	- Door (840 × 2100): lintel 97 × 145, cripple studs 47 × 97, bottom rail cut off after erection; stopper 12 × 40; studs 25 × 100 / 25 × 75 in door framework; 8 mm floor clearance.
320	- Panel type sections: kitchen partition (stud 47 × 97; cemboard 8 + 10 mm → 115 thick); internal partition (stud 47 × 72, ply MR 6 mm b/s → 84); external partition (stud 47 × 97, ply MR 6 inside, WBP 9 outside → 92). Corner details for kitchen and main building with 6/8 mm filler pieces.
321	
322	**Sheet: Platform details (post & entrance stairs; joist stiffeners)**
323	- Joist stiffener layout: 50 × 50 at ends, 50 × 75 mid-span; joists 47 × 145 notched for stiffeners; bearers 2/60 × 194.
324	- Post & bearer detail: bolts 4/15.9 dia through bearers and post; splices 2/10 × 194 × 440 with bolts 15.9 dia (110/110/110 spacing).
325	- Post & entrance stairs section: footing with hardcore 150, concrete, MS bars 12 dia both ways; MS U-strap 6 × 100 fixed to post with 2/12.7 bolts; plate 6 mm; post 120 × 120; stair: treads 47 × 250 on 50 × 50 × 180, stringer 60 × 219, angle iron 63 × 63 × 200 to concrete landing (600 wide, hardcore below), rise 170/run 230.
326	
327	**Sheet: Panel connection details (Drg 101/94/8 of 9)**
328	- Plywood corner panels: plywood beading 2/9 × 72 covers all nail plates; temporary lifting handles one each end.
329	- Elevation of plywood panel connection: 3 knuckle nail plates (Pryda) 2N10 (63 × 89) fixed on exterior side only @ 610 spacing; base plate 47 × 112; plywood skirting 9 × 100 both sides; wall plate 47 × 112 with beading 305 lengths.
330	- Cemboard connections: galvanised metal plate 1 mm thick angle (80 × 80 legs, drilled/punched for 2.5 × 50 nails) for corners; flat 80 × 80 plate joining panels; cemboard beading 5 mm × 100 covers joints; dowel bar 12 × 50 @ 610 crs in curb; conc. curb 50 × 115, conc. floor 100 mm.
331	- **Nailing pattern of panel sheathing:** nails 2.5 × 50; edge distance 12 mm; spacing 150 mm at perimeter, 300 mm intermediate.
332	
333	**Sheet: Truss & roof framing details**
334	- **Truss (View V):** span 5770 between bearings (+28 mm each end), 1923/1924/1923 bottom-chord panel points; height 1195 to apex; top-chord panel points 1442.5; all members 35 × 72; extended rafter 2415 + 520 overhang to kitchen side; splice joint in extended rafter, skew-nailed to wall plate.
335	- **Plywood gusset details:** 9 mm plywood both sides; nails 3.3 × 63; spacing along grain 46 mm, perpendicular to grain 23 mm, edge distance 16 mm; circled numbers = nails per member at each gusset (apex 360 × 220 with 7+7; heel 150 × 100 area with 8; web joints 250 × 200, 180 × 80, 400 × 80, 500 × 80, 380 × 180 with 3–16 nails as tabulated).
336	- **Roof framing plan:** overall 7526 × 5714; trusses 35 × 72 @ 1220 crs (4 × 1220 = 4880 central + 1323 ends); ridge point marked; diagonal braces 22 × 97 in a diamond from gable-truss top to fourth-truss bottom; horizontal braces 22 × 97; kitchen area 4500 wide with additional 35 × 72 beams between extended rafters.
337	
338	---
339	
340	## Construction sequence summary (for procedural modelling)
341	
342	1. **Grid:** everything on a 610 mm module (M = 1220 mm); studs/joists @ 610 crs, trusses @ 1220 crs, all vertically aligned.
343	2. **Set out** 12 footing positions (3 × 2440 by 2 × 2700 grid) with batter boards; square by diagonals.
344	3. **Footings:** 12 pads — hole 600 × 600 × 400, 150 hardcore, ≥300 concrete (1:2:4) topped ≥50 above ground, U-strap cast in.
345	4. **Platform:** posts 120 × 120 × 499 in U-straps → paired bearers 2/60 × 194 bolted both sides of posts → joists 47 × 145 @ 610 slant-nailed, stiffeners 50 × 50 (ends) / 50 × 75 (centre) in notches → T&G floor 22 × 145 blind-nailed → header joist 20 × 194. Platform level 700 above ground.
346	5. **Base plates** 47 × 112 (ext) / 47 × 84 (int) nailed to floor; kitchen uses cast concrete curbs 50 × 115 / 50 × 84 with 12 × 100 anchor bolts instead.
347	6. **Wall panels:** 27 prefab panels (2745 high, ≤2550 long; studs 47 × 97 or 47 × 72; ply 9/6 mm or cemboard 10/8 mm sheathing), erected corner-first with temporary props; fixed with Pryda 2N10 nail plates @ 610 and 3NA corner angles; wall plates 47 × 112 / 22 × 84 bind tops. Non-load-bearing partitions shorter (clearance under trusses).
348	7. **Roof:** gable trusses (35 × 72 members, 9 mm ply gussets, span ~5770, apex 1195) @ 1220 crs; 4 trusses extend 2415+520 over the kitchen; diagonal + horizontal braces 22 × 97; purlins 35 × 72; fascia 20 × 145; corrugated fibre-cement sheets; 6 mm ply gables with vent holes.
349	8. **Doors/windows:** into pre-framed openings (lintels 97 × 145 on cripple studs); doors 700/770/840 × 2100; louvre windows 1055 × 1587 typical.
350	9. **Stairs/railings:** 2 stairs (rise 170/run 230, treads 47 × 250, stringers 60 × 219); railings 1000 high, balusters 20 × 20.
351	10. **Ceiling:** noggings 38 × 50 @ 610 between trusses; 6 mm boards (main building only).
352	11. **Services** in drilled holes/notches per rules; then skirtings 9 × 100, beadings 9 × 72, paint.
353

# Construction Manual of Prefabricated Timber House — Extracted Notes

**Source:** *Construction Manual of Prefabricated Timber House*, FRIM Technical Information Handbook No. 5, by Mohd Shukari Midon, Chu Yue Pun, Hilmi Md Tahir, Nor Azian Mohd Kasby. Forest Research Institute Malaysia (FRIM) / International Tropical Timber Organization (ITTO), 1996. ISBN 983-9592-55-6. Produced under the project "Research on the Utilization of Tropical Timber in Construction". Extracted from `Construction Manual Of Prefabricated Timber House.pdf`.

**Scope:** Step-by-step construction of a prefabricated 'low-cost' single-storey timber-framed house (platform frame method, **Modular Panel System**) designed for Malaysia/tropical climates (not suitable for very strong winds or hurricanes). Panels may be factory-made or assembled on site DIY-style. Internal partitions are non-load-bearing and can be rearranged without affecting structural strength. Appendix contains 9 sheets of detailed technical drawings.

---

## Key dimensions quick reference

| Parameter | Value |
|---|---|
| Module 'M' | 1.22 m (4 ft) — matches local sheet materials |
| Planning grid | 610 mm (dimensions are multiples of 610 mm) |
| Sheet material size | 1220 × 2440 mm (printed "1220 x 2240", evidently a typo) |
| Stud spacing | 610 mm centres |
| Floor joist spacing | 610 mm centres |
| Roof truss spacing | 1220 mm centres (trusses align over studs/joists) |
| Wall panel height (platform area) | 2745 mm (9 ft) floor-to-ceiling |
| Max panel length | ≤3000 mm for man-handling (longest actual panel 2550 mm) |
| Platform height above ground | 700 mm minimum (ventilation) |
| Built-up area | 50 m² proposed house; 63 m² with future extension |
| Main platform footprint | 7320 × 5490 mm (plan); kitchen ~3.1 × 5.1 m at rear on ground |
| Number of wall panels | 21 over platform + 6 over kitchen = 27 total |
| Footings | 12 concrete footings; hole 600 × 600 × 400 mm deep |
| Posts | 120 × 120 × 499 mm high timber on concrete footings |
| Studs | 47 × 97 mm (thicker/exterior panels), 47 × 72 mm (thinner/interior) |
| Floor joists | 47 × 145 mm @ 610 crs |
| Bearers | double 60 × 197 mm (2 per post row; drawings label 2/60 × 194) |
| Floor boards | T&G strip flooring 22 × 145 mm (Ch. 6 text says 30 × 145; Table 1 and drawings say 22 × 145) |
| Truss members | all 35 × 72 mm |
| Purlins | 35 × 72 mm |
| Truss braces | 22 × 97 mm (horizontal and diagonal) |
| Ceiling noggings | 38 × 50 mm @ 610 crs |
| Door widths | 700 (WC/bath), 770 (room/kitchen), 840 (main entrance); all 2100 mm high |
| Stairs | rise 170 mm, run 230 mm; treads 47 × 250 mm |
| Railing height | 1000 mm above floor |
| Sheathing tolerance | 1–3 mm expansion gap between sheets; panel length 1–3 mm under drawing size |
| House height | ~2869 mm to eaves over 700 mm platform (side elevation) |

---

## Chapter 2 — Fabrication systems (overview)

1. **Pre-cut system** — oldest: timber cut/notched/drilled at factory, marked, bundled and assembled on site. More accurate than site cutting, minimal waste.
2. **Modular panel system** *(adopted in this manual, fig. 1)* — components built in factory by 2–3 men without cranes. Uniform wall panels sized on module M = 1.22 m (4 ft) to tally with Malaysian cladding sheets (plywood, hardboard, chipboard, cement board). Exploded view: floor joists → floor panels → wall panels → ceiling panels → roof truss.
3. **Large size panel system** (fig. 2) — panels up to 10–12 m (a dwelling length) factory-assembled; good for mass building many small houses; fewer site joints but higher transport/handling costs and cranes needed.
4. **Volume element system** (fig. 3) — dwellings completely finished at the factory on foundation beams; buyer sees the finished house beforehand; fastest site erection but needs trailers and cranes.

---

## Chapter 3 — Design of the house

- Traditional Malaysian construction is **post and beam** (beams 2–4 m apart on posts; non-load-bearing infill panels). The manual's house is instead **timber-framed (wood-framed)** — traditional in North America/Scandinavia, comparatively new in Malaysia.
- Two timber-frame methods:
  - **Balloon frame** (fig. 4): studs run full building height; intermediate floor joists side-fixed to studs. Only for 2–4 storey buildings.
  - **Platform frame** (fig. 5) — *used here*: shell built one storey at a time with storey-height wall panels; each floor becomes the construction platform for the next storey or roof.
- **Wall panel make-up** (fig. 6): top and bottom horizontal plates spaced for the designed height (2745 mm / 9 ft); vertical studs nailed between them at 610 mm centres (the text's "0.16 m centres" is a misprint — 610 mm everywhere else); noggings added to strengthen sheathing edges; sheets fixed one or both sides. All framework butt-jointed and nailed. Panels ≤3000 mm long for man-handling. Panels erected over the prepared platform, roof placed over to complete the building.
- **Advantages of timber-framed construction:** (1) simple transport of pre-assembled panels; (2) less site labour (more saved if factory-assembled); (3) panels erected manually by 2–3 men, no cranes; (4) speed — all wall panels of a house up in 2–3 days; once roofed, plumbing/electrical proceed in the dry; (5) low-cost high thermal insulation; (6) flexible design, modification and extension.

---

## Chapter 4 — Basic principles

- **Modular dimensioning:** best use of sheet materials + easy later extension. Local sheets are 1220 × 2440 mm, so planning uses multiples of **610 mm**; a 610 mm grid governs plan layout and positioning/fixing of partitions, roofs, joists (fig. 7).
- **Example plan (fig. 7):** proposed house 50 m² (7320 mm frontage × 5490 mm, with kitchen/WC/bath wing 4270 wide × 2440 deep at rear); future extension 3050 mm (bedroom 3) brings it to 63 m². Rooms: BR1, BR2, Living/Dining, Verandah, Kitchen, Bath, WC.
- **Load path (fig. 8):** unlike post-and-beam, the *wall panels are load-bearing*. Roof trusses (@1220 crs), studs (@610 crs) and floor joists (@610 crs) are kept **vertically in line** for efficient load transfer roof → studs → joists → ground. Section shows: roof truss / head binder / top plate / vertical stud / nogging / lintel / cripple stud / door / bottom plate / base plate / floor board / floor joist / bearer.
- **Load-bearing vs non-load-bearing walls (fig. 9):** load-bearing walls support floor/roof above. Non-load-bearing walls are partitions only — made **shorter** than load-bearing walls in the same storey so roof/floor joists above do not rest on them (clearance at top).
- **Openings:** doors/windows need a **lintel** spanning the opening, ends carried on **cripple studs** each side (fig. 8). Small openings need no lintel — simply framed between studs.
- **Panel-making tolerances:**
  1. Stud depth uniform throughout so finished panel-with-sheathing width is constant (e.g. for 47 × 97 studs, the 97 mm dimension must be accurate/regularised).
  2. 1–3 mm vertical gap between plywood sheathings for expansion, covered with beading.
  3. Finished length of each prefabricated panel 1–3 mm less than the drawing size.
- **Detached or linked houses:** houses may be linked by a **separating wall** (fig. 10; grid 305 mm, min 305 mm separating wall zone); empty space between neighbouring houses acts as a firebreak; minimum spacing per Uniform Building By-laws 1984.

### Sequence of construction (summary from Ch. 4)
- Main building at front on a raised platform **700 mm above ground**; kitchen at the back on ground-level concrete. Floor-to-ceiling **2745 mm (9 ft)**. Perspective in fig. 11.
- Order: concrete footings → posts on footings → bearers bolted across posts → floor joists with stiffening cross-pieces on bearers → T&G floor boards conceal-nailed → platform ready. Then pre-assembled wall panels erected over platform (kitchen, on ground level and not connected to the platform, can proceed simultaneously) → head binders/wall plates bind panel tops and support trusses → panels fixed sideways with nailed iron plates/angles, concealed with beading → prefabricated trussed rafter roofs on wall plates → rafters braced diagonally, purlins nailed → roofing sheets (now weathertight) → doors and windows → plumbing, wiring, sanitation → paint → occupy.

---

## Chapter 5 — General requirements and specification of materials

### Timber
- **Strength Group B** per Malaysian Standard M.S. 544:1978 (SIRIM).
- **Grade:** Standard structural grade per Malaysian Grading Rules (MGR) Part III Section J.
- **Sizes:** as drawings. Exposed surfaces planed; unexposed sawn unless regularised (e.g. the 97 mm of 47 × 97 studs must be fixed/accurate).
- **Moisture content at installation:** floor boards ≤ 18%; all other timber ≤ 22%.
- **Preservative treatment:** pressure impregnated with CCA to dry salt retention **5.6 kg/m³**, CCA penetration ≥ **12 mm**.

### Panels/boards
- **Plywood:** from a reputable mill; **WBP** (water-boil-proof) or **MR** (moisture-resistant) type per position in the plan.
- **Cement-bonded particleboard** (cemboard) for kitchen; fix per manufacturer's instructions.
- All other materials per good construction practice.

### Table 1 — Specification and quantities of materials (guide; exact dims in Appendix)

**(A) Platform**
| Item | Part | Material | Size (mm) | Remarks |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A1 | Post | Timber | 120 × 120 | Top of conc. footing |
| A2 | Bearer | Timber | 60 × 197 | Both sides of post |
| A3 | Bearer splice | Timber | 30 × 194 | Lengthen splice |
| A4 | Joist | Timber | 47 × 145 | Top of bearer |
| A5 | Joist stiffener (I) | Timber | 50 × 50 | At end of joist |
| A6 | Joist stiffener (II) | Timber | 50 × 75 | At mid joist |
| A7 | Floor board | Timber | 22 × 145 | T & G |
| A8 | Header joist | Timber | 20 × 194 | Close joist gap |
| A9 | Base plate | Timber | 47 × 112 | Thicker panel |
| A10 | Bolts & nuts | M.S. | 12.7 dia. | Joint fastener |
| A11 | U-strap | M.S. | 6 mm thick | To fix post |
| A12 | Plate | M.S. | 6 mm thick | Bearer for post |
| A13 | Round bar | M.S. | 12.7 dia. | Reinforcement |
| A14 | Conc. footing | Concrete | 1:2:4 mix | Footing for post |
| A15 | Hardcore | Stone | 25 mm size | For conc. |

**(B) Kitchen floor**
| Item | Part | Material | Size (mm) | Remarks |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| B1 | Floor | Concrete | 100 thick | Whole floor |
| B2 | Curb | Concrete | 50 × 115 / 50 × 88 | Thicker / thinner panel |
| B3 | Hardcore | Stone | 25 mm size | For conc. |

**(C) Wall panels**
| Item | Part | Material | Size (mm) | Remarks |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| C1 | Studs (I) | Timber | 47 × 97 | Thicker panel |
| C2 | Studs (II) | Timber | 47 × 72 | Thinner panel |
| C3 | Lintel (I) | Timber | 97 × 145 | Thicker panel |
| C4 | Lintel (II) | Timber | 72 × 145 | Thinner panel |
| C5 | Sheathing (I) | Plywood | 9 mm WBP | Outside surface |
| C6 | Sheathing (II) | Plywood | 6 mm MR | Inside surface |
| C7 | Sheathing (I) | Cemboard | 10 mm | Kitchen outside |
| C8 | Sheathing (II) | Cemboard | 8 mm | Kitchen inside |
| C9 | Beading (I) | Plywood | 9 mm | In strips |
| C10 | Beading (II) | Cemboard | 8 mm | In strips |
| C11 | Pryda nail plate | Product | 63 × 89 | Connection, flat |
| C12 | Pryda angle plate | Product | 44 × 44 × 93 | Connection, corner |
| C13 | Plate w/holes | M.S. | 80 × 80 | Connection, cemboard |
| C14 | Angle plate w/h | M.S. | 48 × 48 × 80 | Cemboard corner |
| C15 | Dowel | M.S. | 12.7 dia. | Embedded in curb |

**(D) Head binder**
